matters.title: Supplemental No. 4: BMW Motorcycle Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) Parts and Repairs
matters.text:
..Title
Supplemental No. 4: BMW Motorcycle Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) Parts and Repairs
..End

..FileID
File ID: 2024-01033
..End

..Location
Location: Citywide
..End

..Recommendation
Recommendation: Pass a Motion authorizing the City Manager or City Manager's designee to execute Supplement No. 4 to Contract No. 2020-2566 with A&S Motorcycle Parts, Inc. for the purchase of BMW Motorcycle original equipment manufacturer (OEM) parts and services increasing the amount of the contract by $150,000 for a revised total contract not-to-exceed amount of $500,000.

..End

..Contact
Contact: Bobbie Small, Program Specialist, (916) 808-6711, bsmall@cityofsacramento.org; Alison Kerstetter, Fleet Manager, (916) 808-1163, akerstetter@cityofsacramento.org; Department of Public Works
..End

..Presenter
Presenter: None.
..End

..Attachments
Attachments: 
1-Description/Analysis
2-Supplemental Agreement No. 4
..End

Description/Analysis
..IssueDetail
Issue Detail: The Department of Public Works, Fleet Management Division, consistently needs to procure BMW Motorcycle original equipment manufacturer (OEM) parts and repair services for the City's BMW Motorcycle fleet. 
..End

..PolicyConsiderations
Policy Considerations: The recommendations in this report are in accordance with City Code Section 3.56.290, which requires City Council approval of supplemental contracts that increase the contract amount beyond the city manager's statutory authority.
..End

..EconomicImpacts
Economic Impacts: None.
..End

..EnvironmentalConsiderations
Environmental Considerations: 

California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA): California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA): No environmental review is necessary because the recommendations in this report involve the purchase of vehicle services and are not considered to be a project in accordance with Section 15378(b)(2) of the California Environmental Quality Act guidelines. 
..End

..Sustainability
Sustainability: Not Applicable
..End

..Commission/Committee Action
Commission/Committee Action: None.
..End

..RationaleforRecommendation
Rationale for Recommendation: The Department of Public Works, Fleet Management Division conducted extensive research to locate an authorized BMW Motorcycle service center capable of providing parts and servicing for the City's BMW Motorcycle fleet. Authorized service centers undergo specialized training by manufacturers to handle parts and repairs for their specific brands of vehicles or equipment. This is critical for maintaining warranty integrity, as repairs and preventative maintenance completed by authorized service centers ensure warranty validity.  The City Council awarded the contract with an initial not-to-exceed amount of $350,000. Three subsequent supplemental contracts extended the time of performance. However, due to a higher rate of utilization than originally projected, the current contract authority is expected to be depleted before the contract term ends. Therefore, Fleet Management Division recommends approving Contract Supplement No. 4 to prevent any service disruptions.
..End

..FinancialConsiderations
Financial Considerations: Sufficient funds are available in the Department of Public Works, Fleet Management Division's, Fiscal Year (FY) 2023/24 operating budget (Fleet Fund, Fund 6501) to purchase BMW Motorcycle original equipment manufacturer (OEM) parts and repairs through June 30, 2024. Purchases made after June 30, 2024, are subject to funding availability in the adopted budget of the applicable fiscal year.

Due to the forecasted structural budget gap, the City Manager has directed City departments to minimize costs and for all new contracts to receive an additional level of scrutiny to ensure they are necessary for the operation of the City. This contract has been reviewed and approved by the City Manager's Office to advance to Council for approval. Funding for the proposed contract beyond FY2023/24 is subject to Council approval.
..End

..LocalBusinessEnterprise
Local Business Enterprise (LBE): A&S Motorcycle Parts, Inc. is not an LBE vendor. The minimum LBE participation requirement was waived by the Director of Public Works. 
Staff conducted an extensive search within the local area and found one authorized service center within a 20-mile radius. 
..End

matters.title: Contract Supplement No. 2: Cummins Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) Parts and Repair Services [Published for 10-day Review on 07/31/2025]
matters.text:
..Title
Contract Supplement No. 2: Cummins Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) Parts and Repair Services [Published for 10-day Review on 07/31/2025]
..End

..FileID
File ID:  2025-01412
..End

..Location
Location: Citywide
..End

..Recommendation
Recommendation: Pass a Motion authorizing the Interim City Manager or designee to execute Supplement No. 2 to Contract 2023-1219 with Dobbs Heavy Duty Holdings LLC, dba Dobbs Truck Group, Inc. for Cummins Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) Heavy Duty Truck Parts and Repair Services in an amount not to exceed $300,000 for a revised total contract not-to-exceed amount of $1,050,000.
..End

..Contact
Contact: Stacey Chatman, Program Specialist, (916) 808-6711, schatman@cityofsacramento.org; Alison Kerstetter, Fleet Manager, (916) 808-1163, akerstetter@cityofsacramento.org; Department of Public Works
..End

..Presenter
Presenter: None
..End

..Attachments
Attachments: 
1-Description/Analysis
2-Contract Supplement No. 2
..End

Description/Analysis
..IssueDetail
Issue Detail: The Department of Public Works, Fleet Management Division, relies on a steady supply of Cummins parts and repair services to maintain the City's fleet. Cummins engines are widely used in heavy-duty vehicles, including dump trucks, fire engines, and refuse trucks making these services essential to daily operations.

To secure a vendor, the City issued an invitation for bids (IFB) on June 5, 2023, with a closing date of June 23, 2023. Four bids were received; however, all were deemed non-responsive for failing to meet the Local Business Enterprise (LBE) participation requirements. Rather than reissue the IFB with an LBE waiver, the City Council passed Motion No. 2023-0253 on September 12, 2023, suspending competitive bidding and awarding a contract to Dobbs Truck Group, Inc. the lowest bidder for Cummins Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) parts and heavy-duty truck repair services. 

Recently, there has been a noticeable increase in the need for Cummins Engine repairs due to unintended part failures and other non-warrantied issues. While this part of a broader industry
trend, and not specific to the City's fleet, it has resulted in higher than anticipated repair costs.  As a result, an increase in the total contract amount is now necessary to ensure continued service availability.
..End

..PolicyConsiderations
Policy Considerations: The recommendations in the report are in accordance with City Code Section 4.04.020 and Council Rules of Procedure, Chapter 7, Section E.2.d., which mandate that unless waived by two-thirds vote of the City Council, all labor agreements, and all agreements greater than $1,000,000 shall be made available to the public at least ten (10) days prior to the City Council action. This item was published for 10-day review on July 31, 2025, in compliance with City Code.
..End

..EconomicImpacts
Economic Impacts: None
..End

..EnvironmentalConsiderations
Environmental Considerations: 

California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA): No environmental review is necessary because the recommendations in this report involves the purchase of parts and services and are not considered to be a project in accordance with Section 15378(b)(2) of the California Environmental Quality Act guidelines. 
      ..End

..Sustainability
Sustainability: Not applicable.
..End

..Commission/Committee Action
Commission/Committee Action: None.
..End

..RationaleforRecommendation
Rationale for Recommendation: On September 12, 2023, the City entered into a contract with Dobbs Heavy Duty Holdings LLC, dba Dobbs Truck Group, Inc. for Cummins Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) heavy duty truck parts and repair services.

The anticipated not-to-exceed amount on the contract is nearing exhaustion due to increased need for parts and services within recent months. There has been a noticeable increase in the need for Cummins Engine repairs due to catastrophic failures and other non-warrantied issues which have increased spending. Staff recommends increasing the current contract by $300,000 to a new not to exceed amount of $1,050,000.
..End

..FinancialConsiderations
Financial Considerations: Sufficient funding exists in the Department of Public Works fiscal year 2025/26 operating budget (Fleet Fund, Fund 6501) for Cummins Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) parts and repair services through June 30, 2026. Purchase of services made after June 30, 2026, are subject to funding availability in the adopted budget of the applicable fiscal year. 
..End

..LocalBusinessEnterprise
Local Business Enterprise (LBE): Dobbs Heavy Duty Holdings LLC, dba Dobbs Truck Group, Inc. is not an LBE. 
..End

matters.title: Contract: BMW Motorcycle Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) Parts and Repairs [Two-Thirds Vote Required]
matters.text:
..Title
Contract: BMW Motorcycle Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) Parts and Repairs [Two-Thirds Vote Required]
..End

..FileID
File ID: 2025-01463
..End

..Location
Location: Citywide
..End

..Recommendation
Recommendation: Pass a Motion by two-thirds: 1) suspending competitive bidding in the best interest of the City for the purchase of BMW Motorcycle Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) Parts and Repairs; 2) awarding an five-year contract to A&S Motorcycle Parts, Inc. in an amount not to exceed $650,000; and 3) authorizing the Interim City Manager or designee to execute the contract specified above provided that sufficient funds are available in the adopted budget for the applicable fiscal years.
..End

..Contact
Contact: Stacey Chatman, Program Specialist, (916) 808-6711; Alison Kerstetter, Fleet Manager, (916) 808-1163, Department of Public Works
..End

..Presenter
Presenter: None
..End

..Attachments
Attachments: 
1-Description/Analysis
2-Contract
..End

Description/Analysis
..IssueDetail
Issue Detail: The Department of Public Works, Fleet Management Division, has an ongoing requirement to purchase BMW Motorcycle Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) parts and repairs for the City's fleet. The City has standardized on BMW Motorcycles for the Police Department Fleet. To service and repair these motorcycles an authorized dealer must be utilized. There are no authorized dealers within the City and only one authorized dealer within the surrounding area. To meet service and repair needs for existing fleet the Department is seeking to suspend competitive bidding and award a five year contract to the closest authorized dealer.
..End

Policy Considerations: The recommendations in this report are in accordance with City Code Chapter 3.56 which authorizes City Council to suspend competitive bidding when, upon a two-thirds vote, it is determined that it is the best interest of the City to do so.

Economic Impacts: None.

Environmental Considerations: California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA): No environmental review is necessary because the recommendations in this report involve the purchase of services and are not considered to be a project in accordance with Section 15378(b)(2) of the California Environmental Quality Act guidelines.

Sustainability: Not applicable.

Commission/Committee Action: None.

Rationale for Recommendation: The Department of Public Works, Fleet Management Division has completed extensive research to find an authorized BMW Motorcycle service center to issue parts and complete repairs for the BMW Motorcycle fleet within the City. Authorized service centers are trained by manufacturers to provide parts and repairs for the specific brand of vehicles or equipment. This is especially important as the warranty stays intact when authorized service centers complete repairs and services.  The Department has previously solicited bids for service and repair of BMW motorcycles and it has typically yielded only one bidder, A&S Motorcycle Parts, Inc.  Upon preparing for a new contract this year research was conducted through BMW and A&S Motorcycle Parts, Inc is the only authorized dealer within a reasonable distance. The next closest location is in Concord.
A&S Motorcycle Parts, Inc. is the only authorized dealer within a 20-mile radius of the City. Fleet Management recommends awarding the contract to A&S Motorcycle Parts, Inc. as they are the closest authorized dealer.

Financial Considerations: Sufficient funding exists in the Department of Public Works Fiscal Year (FY) 2025/26 operating budget (Fleet Fund, Fund 6501) to purchase BMW Motorcycle OEM parts and repairs through June 30, 2026. Purchases made after June 30, 2026, are subject to funding availability in the adopted budget of the applicable fiscal year.

The recommended contract amount of $650,000 reflects the amount anticipated to be expended over the five-year contract period. 

Local Business Enterprise (LBE): A&S Motorcycle Parts, Inc. is not an LBE vendor. The minimum LBE participation requirement was waived by the Director of Public Works. Staff conducted an extensive search within the local area and found one authorized service center within a 20-mile radius.

..Recommendation
Recommendation: Pass a Motion authorizing the City Manager or designee to execute Supplemental Contract No. 2 to Contract No. 2024-0929 with Suburban Motors dba Future Ford of Sacramento increasing the contract amount by $4,800,000, for a revised contract not-to-exceed amount of $6,000,000 and extending the time of performance through June 25, 2029.
..End

..Contact
Contact: Stacey Chatman, Program Specialist, (916) 808-6711, schatman@cityofsacramento.org; Alison Kerstetter, Fleet Manager, (916) 808-1163, akerstetter@cityofsacramento.org; Department of Public Works
..End

..Presenter
Presenter: None
..End

..Attachments
Attachments: 
1-Description/Analysis
2-Supplemental Contract No. 2
..End

Description/Analysis
..IssueDetail
Issue Detail: The Fleet Management Division of the Department of Public Works oversees purchasing, maintenance, and repair services for all City fleet assets. To maintain warranties and ensure safety and reliability, the City uses authorized service centers and Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) parts. Future Ford, the current Ford vendor, provides these services (based on the award of the City's solicitation B24153311009). Because the City has standardized on the Ford brand for efficiency, Ford vehicles now make up 45% of the fleet. To keep parts and services available and accommodate the growing number of Ford vehicles, the contract must be increased to cover the remaining term of the agreement, June 25, 2029.
..End

..PolicyConsiderations
Policy Considerations: The recommendations in this report are in accordance with City Code Chapter 3.56.090, which requires City Council approval for contracts with expenditures exceeding $250,000. 

Sacramento City Code Section 4.04.020 and the City Council Rules of Procedure (Chapter 7 Section E.2.d) mandate that unless waived by a 2/3 vote of the City Council, all labor agreements, and all agreements greater than $1,000,000 shall be made available to the public at least 10 days prior to City Council action. This item was published for 10-day review on February 19, 2026, in compliance with the City Code.
..End

..EconomicImpacts
Economic Impacts: None.
..End

..EnvironmentalConsiderations
Environmental Considerations: 
California Environmental Quality Act Guidelines: No environmental review is necessary because the recommendations in this report involve the purchase of services and is not considered to be a project in accordance with Section 15378(b)(2) of the California Environmental Quality Act guidelines.
..End

..Sustainability
Sustainability: The recommended purchases are consistent with the updated Fleet Sustainability Policy adopted by City Council on December 12, 2017 (Resolution No. 2017-0478) and California Air Resource Board (CARB) regulations. 
..End

..Commission/CommitteeAction
Commission/Committee Action: None.
..End

..RationalforRecommendation
Rationale for Recommendation: On March 26, 2024, Fleet Management posted solicitation B24153311009 in search of contracting with OEM Ford providers. An RFP was utilized, rather than a competitive bid process, as it was in the City's best interest to consider capacity, performance, and timeliness of service in addition to price. Three submittals were received, two deemed responsive. Given the number of Ford assets, both bidders were awarded a contract at the June 25, 2024 City Council meeting with Motion 2024-0202. The City Council suspended competitive bidding as being in the best interest of the City. Future Ford is the most responsive and efficient when vehicles are sent out for service so this contract has been expended at a higher rate than anticipated and needs to be increased to ensure continuation of services. Staff is requesting that City Council vest the City Manager or designee with the power to effectuate the increase not-to-exceed amount identified.
..End

..FinancialConsiderations
Financial Considerations: Purchases made under this contract will be made from the Department of Public Works Fiscal Year (FY) 2025/26 operating budget (Fleet Fund, Fund 6501) and will be charged to the using Department upon purchase. Sufficient funding exists in the Department's FY2025/26 operating budget to support the recommended purchase.
..End

..LocalBusinessEnterprise(LBE)
Local Business Enterprise (LBE): Future Ford of Sacramento is an LBE vendor.
..End

..Title
[Contract Amendment] Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) Parts and Services
..End

..FileID
File ID: 2026-00933
..End

..Location
Location: Citywide
..End

..Recommendation
Recommendation: Pass a Motion authorizing the City Manager or designee to execute Contract Amendment No. 1 to Contract PRC004024 with Municipal Maintenance Equipment, Inc. (MME) for the purchase of Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) parts and services for Schwarze, VacCon, Tiger and Pipehunter equipment, increasing the contract amount by $500,000 for a revised contract total not-to-exceed amount of $700,000.
..End

..Contact
Contact: Stacey Chatman, Program Specialist, (916) 808-6711, schatman@cityofsacramento.org; Alison Kerstetter, Fleet Manager, (916) 808-1163, akerstetter@cityofsacramento.org; Department of Public Works
..End

..Presenter
Presenter: None
..End

..Attachments
Attachments: 
1-Description / Analysis
2-Contract Amendment No. 1 
..End

Description/Analysis
..IssueDetail
Issue Detail: The Department of Public Works, Fleet Management Division, manages all City fleet assets from acquisition through maintenance and final decommissioning. To reduce costs and simplify repairs, Fleet standardizes equipment whenever possible and prioritizes the use of local vendors for parts and services.
The City's fleet includes one Schwarze street sweeper, twelve VacCon sewer cleaning units, one Tiger mower, and six Pipehunter sewer jetters. A single vendor-MME-is the authorized parts and service provider for all these manufacturers, as reflected in Agreement PRC004024 for OEM support.  Although the City is transitioning away from the Schwarze and Tiger lines, continued support for these units remains necessary.

Contract PRC004024, executed on February 1, 2026, established a five-year, $200,000 not-to-exceed amount for parts and services. However, after reviewing equipment usage and customer needs, Fleet has determined that the current budget is insufficient due to the high cost of parts and repair work for these specialized units.

Additionally, MME is the only vendor offering rental VacCon equipment, which is essential when units are out of service or when short-term operational demands increase. To ensure uninterrupted sewer maintenance capacity, staff recommend expanding the contract scope to include rental services and increasing the not-to-exceed amount.
..End

..PolicyConsiderations
Policy Considerations: The recommendations in this report are in accordance with City Code
Chapter 3.56, which requires that the City Council approve any activities of $250,000 or more.
..End

..EconomicImpacts
Economic Impacts: None.
..End

..EnvironmentalConsiderations
Environmental Considerations: 
California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA): No environmental review is necessary because the recommendations in this report involve the purchase of fleet equipment and related services which are not considered to be a project in accordance with Section 15378(b)(2) of the California Environmental Quality Act guidelines. 
..End

..Sustainability
Sustainability: Not applicable.
..End

..Commission/Committee Action
Commission/Committee Action: None.
..End

..RationaleforRecommendation
Rationale for Recommendation: In February 2026, the Fleet Management Division entered into a sole-source agreement with MME in the amount of $200,000 for the purchase of parts and services for Schwarze, VacCon, Tiger, and Pipehunter equipment. MME is the only local authorized dealer supporting all four manufacturers.

Since execution of the agreement, additional operational needs have been identified. Rental VacCon units are required when equipment is out of service for repairs outside of warranty and during periods of increased operational demand. MME is the only local authorized vendor that provides rental VacCon equipment.

To ensure the continued availability of parts, service, and rental equipment necessary to support sewer maintenance operations, an amendment to expand the contract scope and increase the not-to-exceed amount by $500,000 for a new not-to-exceed total of $700,000 is recommended for the remainder of the five-year term, ending January 31, 2031.
..End

..FinancialConsiderations
Financial Considerations: Sufficient funding exists in the Department of Public Works, Fleet Management Division, FY2025/26 Approved Operating Budget (Fleet Fund, Fund 6501) to execute the contract supplement. Purchases made after June 30, 2026, are subject to funding availability in the adopted budget of the applicable fiscal year. 
..End

..LocalBusinessEnterprise
Local Business Enterprise (LBE): Municipal Maintenance Equipment, Inc. (MME) is an LBE.
..End
